artboards.title: As it stands today — the Overview, with its eight faults marked
Proposed — the Overview: a verdict, an action, the position, the evidence
Proposed — one of the four statements, with the records rail kept as it is
Proposed — the phone, a reading fallback

annotations.text:
THE BRIEF, AND WHAT YOU SETTLED

You asked for the Statements page designed from first principles, the most professional way imaginable. Six questions, six answers, and everything on this canvas follows from them.

1. FOUR READERS, NOT ONE. You, monthly, judging the shop. A bank or loan officer. An accountant at year end. A manager. That is the tension the whole design turns on: the owner wants a verdict, the bank wants a document. The answer is not a compromise between them -- it is that OVERVIEW IS THE VERDICT AND THE FOUR STATEMENTS ARE THE PACK. Print all five is what leaves the building.

2. THE PHONE IS A READING FALLBACK. Not a second full design. Where you stand, what is wrong with the figures, and the four headline numbers. The charts, the arithmetic and the records stay on the desk, and the phone says so.

3. THE FIVE TABS STAY; THE OVERVIEW GETS FIXED. It was a digest that had grown into a seventh statement, including a second profit and loss with different line names.

4. CUSTOM DATES MATTER AS MUCH AS THE PRESETS. So both keep equal weight -- the segmented control and the range sit side by side, and neither is folded away.

5. ABOVE THE FOLD: CAN THESE BE TRUSTED, THE FOUR VITALS, AND BREAK-EVEN. The trend chart is kept but demoted. Nothing is deleted.

6. THE RECORDS RAIL STAYS EXACTLY AS IT IS, empty invitation included. Your call, and it is drawn here unchanged in behaviour -- only its type and radius come onto the system.

Every value on this canvas is lifted from index.html: the 23-colour palette, the 11/12/13/14/16/20 ramp, Inter + Archivo Black + IBM Plex Mono, and the .ow-* console components already shipping on Today, Debtors, Chase debts, Follow-ups, Consignment, Creditors, Pricing and Analysis. No new colour, no new weight, no new size, no fourteenth button family.

The figures are a worked August 2026 and the arithmetic holds: 148,600,000 sold less 118,880,000 of goods is 29,720,000 gross; less 7,745,000 of running costs is 21,975,000 operating; less 1,050,000 of interest is 20,925,000 net, which is 14.1% of what was invoiced. Break-even is 7,745,000 over a 20.0% margin -- 38,725,000 of sales. The five listed invoices plus the 114,275,000 held back come to 148,600,000 exactly.

WHAT IS WRONG WITH IT TODAY >
The eight circles on the artboard. Every one is checkable in index.html.

1. THE PAGE HAS NO SUB LINE AT ALL. The whole 240-character paragraph is folded behind the "i" bubble, and nothing is left in its place. Eight other screens keep one line visible; the design system says the sub is never folded. Here the reader gets a page name and nothing else -- not even which period is on screen.

2. SEVENTEEN CONTROLS IN TWO STACKED ROWS, INSIDE THE CONTENT PANEL. Five tabs, three presets, two dates, a comparison select and two print buttons, all in one bordered box with the figures. Nothing separates "which document" from "which period" from "put it on paper", and Print sits at the same weight as a date.

3. A PANEL AROUND A PANEL AROUND A PANEL. The whole screen is one .panel -- 12px radius, its own border, its own shadow -- and inside it every block draws another border. Break-even is three grey boxes inside a bordered box inside that panel: three levels of container for three figures. The .ow-strip exists for exactly this and uses hairline dividers with no per-tile border.

4. GOOD NEWS GETS THE LOUDEST DEVICE ON THE SCREEN. The verdict is a full-width tinted slab, 1,090px of verdigris every healthy month. It becomes furniture, and when it turns crimson for a real problem it reads as the same furniture in another colour. The design system's own rule: a device that marks everything marks nothing.

5. THE CHART IS STRETCHED. A 100x46 viewBox drawn with preserveAspectRatio="none" into a 1,058x120 box -- the bars are scaled 10.6x horizontally and 2.6x vertically, and the zero line only survives because it carries vector-effect. With no invoiced sales it draws six pairs of hairlines that look like a broken chart rather than an empty one.

6. THE ORDER CONTRADICTS THE PRIORITY. You named trust, the vitals and break-even as the three that matter. Today the four vitals -- the position in four figures -- sit 620px down, below a chart and a break-even block, and the trust checks are 880px down at the bottom of one of five tabs.

7. THE OVERVIEW CONTAINS A SECOND PROFIT AND LOSS. "Where the profit went" is a mini P&L with different line names from the real one ("Less what the goods cost" against "Cost of sales"). Two versions of the same statement, worded differently, is how two figures that should agree stop agreeing in a reader's head.

8. THE TYPE AND THE RADII ARE OFF THE SYSTEM. The .st-* block has SIXTEEN font sizes, seven of them off the ramp: 9, 9.5, 10.5, 11.5, 12.5, 15.5 and 29px. Eight radii -- 2, 6, 9, 10, 11, 12, 99, 999 -- of which two are on the scale. Twenty-three declarations at weight 700 and four at 600, so nothing is ever merely emphasised. And one box-shadow on the active tab that is not --ow-lift: a second elevation, on a tab.

AND THE ONE THE ARTBOARD CANNOT SHOW: THE PHONE IS THIS PAGE REFLOWED. 2,314px of scroll, the five tab pills wrapped onto two rows, native date inputs squeezed to 12px, and a ratios grid of fourteen cells at 390. The two-designs law says 820px is a switch between two designs, not a reflow of one.

WHAT I HAVE NOT DECIDED FOR YOU

1. WHAT THE VERDICT SAYS WHEN NOTHING IS WRONG. Drawn here in its amber state, because that is the state worth designing. The settled state should be one ink sentence with no button and no colour -- but you may want it to carry something instead of merely being quiet, the way Analysis carries "the thinnest line you sold". Say what that figure is and it goes in.

2. THE TRUST CHECKS ARE NOT RANKED. Four checks in the rail, in the order the app produces them. If one of them is always the one you act on, it should lead and the others should fold.

3. PRINT IS STILL TWO BUTTONS. "Print this" and "Print all five" sit side by side as ghosts. If the printed pack is what a bank actually receives, Print all five deserves to be a real control rather than the quieter of two -- but that would put a second oxide on the screen, so it is a choice between the two, not both.

4. THE PHONE'S FOURTH TAB, "Dates". I have not drawn what it opens. A native date picker is the honest cheap answer; a month grid is the good one.

5. THE RATIOS SCREEN IS UNTOUCHED. Its 14 cells carry four font sizes that are all off the ramp and a 9px uppercase pill that fails contrast at that size. It needs the same pass this Overview got, and it is the one place I would spend the next hour.

6. EMPTY AND FAILED STATES ARE NOT DRAWN. A month with no invoices, and a period where the ledger fails to read, are different news and the app's own law says a failure must name itself. Today both show the same zeros. That is a third artboard whenever you want it.

7. WHAT I HAVE NOT TOUCHED: every figure-producing function, the drill machinery, the print sheet, and the comparison basis logic. The old names stay as search keywords: statements, profit, loss, balance sheet, cash flow, accounts, ratios.

THE PROPOSAL -- what changed, and why

THE SCREEN IS THREE BANDS, AND EACH ANSWERS A DIFFERENT QUESTION. The page header answers WHEN: the name, the period in words, and the period controls with the presets and the custom range at equal weight, the way Payroll carries its month. The document strip answers WHICH: five names on a hairline, the current one underscored in steel, with Print this and Print all five at the far end where the acting happens. Then the content. The .panel that wrapped the whole screen is gone -- it was a box drawn around a page.

THE VERDICT IS A SENTENCE WITH A BUTTON, NOT A SLAB. One line naming the problem in the reader's terms, one line of consequence, one amber mark, and the accent: Invoice the counter sales. That is the only oxide on the screen and the only thing to do next. When nothing is wrong the row says so in ink with no button, and the screen has no accent -- which is correct, because there is nothing to do.

WHY THAT SENTENCE LEADS. 19% of what the shop took in August is outside every figure below it. A reader who learns that after scrolling past a profit figure has already believed the wrong number. The old screen said it too -- in a green slab, above a chart, with the detail 880px lower.

THE POSITION IS THE HOUSE STRIP. Four tiles, hairline dividers, no per-tile borders, mono tabular figures with the unit at 0.55em. It sits directly under the verdict because it is what the verdict qualifies.

THEN TWO COLUMNS, AND THE SPLIT IS BY KIND. On the left, the two things about THIS PERIOD: what August had to cover, and how six months of it look. On the right, in the 304px rail, the two things about the FIGURES THEMSELVES: whether they can be trusted, and what the shop leans on. The trust panel is where the verdict's detail lives, so the headline and the evidence are on one screen instead of 880px apart.

THE MINI PROFIT AND LOSS IS GONE. It was a second statement of the same thing under different names. Its job -- "how did the month go" -- is done better by the net profit tile with its margin, and its detail is one tab away, wording intact.

COLOUR ONLY WHERE IT MEANS SOMETHING. Three marks on the whole desktop: one amber triangle on the verdict, one amber triangle on the check it refers to, one oxide button. Everything else is ink on paper and hairlines. The verdigris tick on the supplier check is the one piece of good news that is genuinely evidence rather than decoration.

THE CHART IS DRAWN AT ITS OWN SIZE. 792x104 css pixels, no non-uniform scaling, bars aligned to the month labels under them, and the zero line placed where zero actually is rather than at the vertical middle -- so June's loss reads as the small loss it was instead of half the panel.

HEIGHT: 1,224px of Overview becomes 1,010px, and that 1,010px now contains the verdict, its action, the position, break-even, six months, four trust checks and the concentration. On a 1440x900 desk everything except the last rail panel is above the fold.

WHAT I DID NOT TOUCH: statementsContext, incomeStatement, balanceSheet, cashFlowStatement, statementChecks, statementBasisGap, breakevenPosition, the drill-down machinery, printStatements or the print stylesheet. This is a design, not a rewrite -- the same readings feed it, and Print all five still puts what is on screen onto paper, reconciliation checks included.

THE FOUR STATEMENTS -- profit and loss, drawn >

THE DOCUMENT IS A PANEL WITH A 34px HEADER, like every other bordered region in the console: the statement's name, its dates, and the count of records behind it. The reading column is capped so the labels never run the width of a 1440 screen, and the two figure columns are sized to their content -- money never gives way, names do. Every figure is mono and tabular, so the column reads down as a column.

THE RECORDS RAIL IS UNCHANGED, AS YOU ASKED. Same behaviour, same width, same empty invitation before anything is clicked, same footer tripwire. What changed is only that its type is on the ramp -- 11/12/20 instead of 10/11.5/12.5/19 -- and its radius is 8 rather than 12. It is drawn here in the state that justifies its width: revenue open, five invoices, and the 57 it is holding back named with what they are worth. The app's own law is that a truncated list says how many it dropped.

THE FOOTER IS THE BEST THING ON THE SCREEN AND IT STAYS. "The 62 invoices add to 148,600,000, which is the figure on the line." With no general ledger behind these statements, that reconciliation is what stands in for a trial balance, and it is the reason an accountant can use this page at all.

THE DRILLED LINE IS MARKED IN OXIDE-SOFT, not a border or a shadow. One row, tinted, with its chevron turned -- the same device the rest of the app uses for an open row.

THE ARROWS WHISPER. A chevron at full ink on thirty rows would shout that everything is a door; at --ow-ink-400 it teaches a first-time reader without shouting at the tenth. That was already right and is kept.

BALANCE SHEET, CASH FLOW AND RATIOS take the same shape and are not drawn here -- one document artboard settles the pattern, and drawing four would be four chances to let them drift apart. The ratios screen is the one that needs a second look, because its 14 cells carry four sizes that are all off the ramp.

THE PHONE -- a reading fallback, and honest about it >

You said a reading fallback, so this is not the desktop competing at 390. It is drawn from scratch: 44px navy bar, 26px Archivo page name, 15px body, 14-16px padding, cards instead of rows, a white 60px tab bar with the active tab FILLED rather than merely coloured. No fake status bar and no fake keyboard -- the real ones render on top of this.

IT FITS IN 844px WITH NO SCROLL. The current screen is 2,314px of reflowed desktop.

THE PERIOD IS ONE 44px CONTROL. Month, Quarter, Year and Dates -- four cells, each a real thumb target, with the range spelled out in words above them. The desktop's two native date inputs at 12px are not a phone control; a fourth cell that opens a picker is.

THE SAME VERDICT AND THE SAME ACTION. One card, the amber mark, and the oxide button at full width in the thumb zone. One accent on the screen, on the top card, because the top of the screen IS the thing to do next.

THE POSITION IS 2x2 IN ONE CARD with hairline dividers and no per-tile borders -- the house pattern, and the same four figures the desk shows.

THEN THE FOUR STATEMENTS AS FOUR ROWS, each carrying its headline figure. This is the whole argument for a phone fallback: you can stand in the yard and know net profit, net worth, the till movement and the gross margin without opening a document. Tapping one takes you to the document; the header says plainly that it is read in full on the desk.

WHAT IS DROPPED, DELIBERATELY: the six-month chart, break-even, the concentration, the trust checks in full, the records rail and printing. A balance sheet at 390px is genuinely hard to read and pretending otherwise is how the current screen ended up 2,314px long.
